transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Nora Patel (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Greenstream Head of Data), Dr. Marcus Hill (CTO), Priya Nair (Security & Compliance), Samir Kahn (Platform)

Summary: POC scoping focused on data handling for a 2-week pilot. Main concerns: PII in prompts, logging and redaction, retention settings, where prompts are stored (auditability vs privacy), and success criteria for benchmarks (latency, throughput, quality). Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted, VPC/private deployment, KMS for key management, and timeline + next steps.

Topics: PII/redaction, retention policy, prompt storage, logging, benchmarks, success criteria, deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated/private), timeline

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick off, quick intro from redwood side, carlos will cover the technical approach and benchmarks, nora will help with onboarding and SSO bits
00:18 Lena (Greenstream): thanks maya, we appreciate it. high level — we want to run a two week poc to validate privacy controls and perf for our triage assistant. key constraints are PHI handling and audit logs, so that's the main reason we reached out
00:35 Carlos (Redwood SE): great, quick clarifying q, when you say PHI are we talking full medical notes, or tokenized identifiers, or both?
00:45 Lena: mostly clinical notes with patient names, MRN, free text. we'll try to sanitize for the sample but we need to confirm redaction and logging behavior on real traffic
01:04 Priya (Greenstream): and i want to flag compliance — we need proof of no persistent storage of raw prompts containing PHI unless encrypted and retained per our retention policy. SOC two is required, also SSO/SAML integration for audit trails
01:24 Maya: totally — we have Redwood Private for VPC/on‑prem, and Dedicated for reserved capacity. for short poc we often run dedicated with strict logging configs, but we can prototype with hosted and limited retention — carlos will outline specifics
01:40 Carlos: ok, benchmark goals first — what success looks like: p95 latency under 500ms for completion only, throughput of ~50 reqs/sec (avg payload ~250 tokens), quality baseline compared to your current heuristics. plus: no unredacted PHI stored in logs and ability to pull audit logs for every request
02:05 Dr. Marcus (CTO): 500ms p95 seems ambitious, we care more about p50 latency for interactive UX and p95 for SLAs. also cost per 1M tokens will matter for long term — can you estimate later?
02:23 Maya: we'll include cost estimates. for the poc we focus on configuration that meets your latency and retention needs; the optimize tool will recommend batching/quant profiles to hit cost targets while keeping quality
02:38 Samir (Platform): question on prompt storage: does Redwood persist full prompts or only prompt hashes? we need to avoid storing raw PHI in plaintext
02:49 Carlos: by default we log requests for debugging but we support redaction and retention settings. options: 1) disable request logging, 2) store only hashed prompts and metadata, 3) encrypt logs with customer KMS, 4) run in Private mode where logs never leave your VPC. we can also redact entities via regex/KV cache filters before persisting
03:18 Priya: can you do field-level redaction automatically? our dataset has many variations of identifiers
03:25 Carlos: we have configurable pre‑processor hooks that can run regex or custom lambda to mask PHI before sending to persistence. note — the transcription on our side sometimes mislabels fields, but the preprocessor runs before logs are written
03:40 Lena: ok for the poc we'll try two approaches: share a sanitized sample and also test on small slice of real traffic behind our VPC with encryption
03:51 Maya: timeline proposal: week1 — run benchmarks on sanitized sample in hosted/dedicated variants; week2 — run private/VPC flow for end‑to-end audit and retention verification. total 2 weeks
04:05 Dr. Marcus: what about model versions? we need to test a couple of model sizes for latency/cost tradeoffs
04:12 Carlos: yes we'll test one LLA‑medium variant and a smaller quantized variant; measure tokens/sec, kv cache behavior on sequence length ~400 tokens. we'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and token cost
04:28 Priya: audit logs — can you produce immutable logs with S3 + glacier style retention and object-level encryption with our KMS?
04:36 Carlos: yes, logs can be exported to your S3 bucket and encrypted with customer KMS; we can also set lifecycle rules for retention. in Private deployments the control plane still produces audit logs that you can ship to your SIEM
04:52 Maya: for access control we support RBAC and SSO via SAML/OIDC; we'll add nora to help with the SSO connector and a checklist for your identity team
05:05 Nora (Redwood CSM): i'll send the SSO checklist and the onboarding doc after this call
05:12 Samir: curious about request-level retention — if we set retention to 7 days then logs are purged; how do you guarantee deletion?
05:20 Carlos: we support retention windows enforced at storage layer and will provide deletion proofs; for hosted we run a scheduled purge job and can provide ledger entries; for private you can run your own retention policies in your bucket
05:36 Priya: need clarity on where prompts are stored for model tuning or debugging. do you store prompts for future fine‑tuning or only ephemeral caching?
05:44 Carlos: by default we don't retain prompts for model training unless you opt in. there's a separate opt-in for long‑term storage for evals. default is ephemeral KV cache in memory and optional short term logs per retention policy
06:02 Lena: okay about the short term cache — for our triage flows we use a lot of prefix caching so keV cache behaviour matters (sic) — will that leak prior prompts to other requests?
06:12 Carlos: no, KV cache is per session/instance, not shared between tenants. that said, concurrency and sharding patterns can influence cache hit rates; we'll include those details in the benchmark plan
06:28 Dr. Marcus: are there any regulatory blockers for PHI with hosted mode? we might need Private for guaranteed network isolation
06:34 Maya: if you require network isolation and customer‑managed keys then Private makes sense; Dedicated can be isolated at tenant level but still runs on our control plane. we'll map requirements to the right deployment
06:50 Priya: encryption at rest and in transit — do you support HSM-backed KMS?
06:55 Carlos: yes, HSM/KMS integrations supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports envelope encryption with our managed keys, or you can bring your own KMS for logs and backups
07:12 Lena: for the POC success criteria, here's what we'd like to see: 1) p95 < 700ms for our main flow, 2) zero exposed PHI in persisted logs, 3) audit logs for every request accessible in our S3, 4) quality >= current rule-based accuracy on triage labels
07:34 Maya: we'll codify that as the acceptance criteria. carlos will produce the benchmark spec mapping metrics and sample traffic
07:44 Carlos: benchmark spec — i'll run: 20k synthetic requests (sanitized) first pass, then 5k requests from real traffic within your VPC. measure p50/p95, throughput, token cost, and false positive/negative on triage labels
08:03 Samir: can we do load from our region? latency from EU matters for some clinics
08:10 Maya: yes we can spin up regionally; note that model availability and quantization profiles vary by region but we'll note it in the bench report
08:23 Priya: about logs — if redaction isn't perfect we need the option to truncate prompts in logs entirely, even if that reduces debuggability
08:33 Carlos: agreed, we can set log level to metadata-only (hashes, timings, model used) and disable full request capture. for debugging we can enable ephemeral logs and then purge after triage
08:48 Lena: what about prompt templates and storage in the console — who can view them and where are they stored?
08:53 Nora: prompt templates are stored in the console by default, with RBAC controls; we can mark templates as sensitive which encrypts their content with your KMS key and restricts viewing
09:05 Priya: are there any known transcription or tokenization gotchas where PHI might be split and bypass regexes?
09:12 Carlos: yes — tokenization can split identifiers unpredictably; we recommend multi‑layer redaction (regex + named entity recognition) and sanity checks in the preprocessor. we'll include recommended regex patterns
09:28 Dr. Marcus: estimation on time to run the benchmark and get results?
09:33 Carlos: for synthetic runs we can produce initial perf report in 48 hours from sample receipt; the VPC/real traffic phase depends on onboarding (SSO, S3 access) but plan is 3–5 business days once credentials provided
09:48 Maya: commercial ask — for a 2‑week pilot we can offer a discounted Dedicated block; i'll send pricing matrix. if Private required we'll need procurement lead time
09:59 Priya: procurement note — we'll need DPA + security addendum and SOC2 before production
10:05 Maya: yes we'll attach our DPA and SOC2 report; nora will start the security doc packet
10:12 Carlos: technical note — we'll output benchmark artifacts (traces, flamegraphs, token breakdown) to a shared folder. we can also produce per‑request audit rows with hashed prompt ids and model signatures
10:28 Lena: ok good. for acceptance finally, can you include an automated check that asserts no persisted prompt contains an unredacted patient name?
10:35 Carlos: yes we can include a small verification script that scans logs for PHI patterns and provides pass/fail as part of the bench report
10:48 Maya: recap and next steps — carlos will send benchmark plan + sample spec, maya will send pricing + pilot contract, nora will send SSO checklist and security packet. greenstream to provide sanitized sample + list of retention policies
10:58 Priya: we'll get the sample and policies over by friday. also we'll add security folks to next call
11:06 Maya: thanks all. meeting adjourned.

Action items (in transcript):
- Carlos: benchmark plan and metrics, produce synthetic + VPC phase plan
- Maya: pricing and pilot contract
- Nora: SSO checklist and security docs

References mentioned: Redwood Private, Dedicated, Redwood Console, Optimize; will share SOC2, DPA, benchmark spreadsheet link (placeholder: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/GS-POC)

Notes on transcription: minor mislabels and filler words present; proper nouns occasionally garbled (LLA‑medium transcribed as "L L A medium"), some punctuation and speaker attribution may be imperfect
